Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:33: And in Ta'anit (7b) they said, rain is withheld only because of the brazen-faced, as it is said (Jeremiah 3:3), "and the showers have been withheld," and so on, "and you had a harlot's forehead," and so on. Rav Hamnuna said, anyone who has a brazen face will eventually stumble into sin, for it does not say "he shall be" [future], but "was" [past tense, indicating a fixed trait]. Rabbah bar Rav Huna said, one may call him wicked to his face. Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said, one may hate him, as it is said (Ecclesiastes 8:1), "the boldness of his face shall be changed [hated]" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:34: It is fitting to be careful of all the things they said in Shabbat (page 32), "because of such-and-such sin, this comes about," and because of the length, we have not copied it, and shall copy only one of them, the one found most commonly: the sin causing the death of children. Rabbi says, because of the sin of vows, their sons and daughters die while young, as it is said (Ecclesiastes 5:5), "do not let your mouth cause your flesh to sin," and so on, as we copied in the Gate of Holiness (chapter 17), and so too is the view of Rabbi Elazar the son of Rashbi (Shabbat, ibid.). And some say, because of the sin of neglecting Torah; and some say, because of the sin of neglecting the mezuzah; and some say, because of the sin of neglecting tzitzit - and all brought proof from verses.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:35: Further, there it is taught: Rabbi Nechemiah says, because of the sin of baseless hatred, great strife arises within a person's household, and his wife miscarries, and his sons and daughters die while young - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:36: And in Pesikta Rabbati (Yalkut Yirmiyah, section 267, page 60c), they said that the essential cause of children's death is neglect of Torah, in these words: Rabbi Meir says, at the time Israel stood before Mount Sinai, the Holy One, blessed be He, said to them, bring Me guarantors that you will keep the Torah, and I will give it to you. They said to Him, our fathers are our guarantors. He said to them, I have claims against your fathers - Abraham, for saying (Genesis 15:8), "how shall I know that I shall inherit it?"; Isaac, for loving Esau; Jacob, for saying (Isaiah 40:27), "my way is hidden [from the LORD]." They said to Him, our children are our guarantors. "Out of the mouths of babes and sucklings You have established strength" (Psalms 8:3) - and "strength" [oz] is nothing but Torah, as it is said (ibid. 29:11), "the LORD will give strength to His people." At the time the borrower is seized [for non-payment] and has nothing to pay, who is seized? Is it not the guarantor? So (Hosea 4:6), "you have forgotten the Torah of your God; I will also forget your children" - as it were, I too shall suffer loss. Who says "Barchu" [call to prayer] before Me? Is it not the children? So (Jeremiah 2:30), "in vain have I struck your children" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:37: Further, they said in the Sifrei (Parashat Ekev, section 10): "and you shall teach them to your sons" - not your daughters, [these are] the words of Rabbi Yosi ben Akiva. From here they said, when a child begins to speak, his father should speak to him in the holy tongue and teach him Torah - and if he does not speak to him in the holy tongue and teach him Torah, it is as though he had buried him, as it is said (Deuteronomy 11:19), "and you shall teach them to your sons... that your days may be multiplied, and the days of your children" - and if not, that your days shall be shortened, and the days of your children - for so words of Torah are expounded: from the affirmative you infer the negative - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:38: And on the virtue of one who speaks in the holy tongue, it is explained in the Zohar (Parashat Noach, page 74b), that the generation of the Dispersion did not succeed in their deeds except because they spoke in the holy tongue - in these words: the secrets of the Torah say that the "confederacy of the ruler" [kimtora d'harmana] speak in the holy tongue, and the ministering angels recognize it, and would not speak in another language - and therefore, "and now nothing will be withheld from them," and so on (Genesis 11:6) - for had they spoken in another language, the supernal angels would not have recognized it, and their scheme to accomplish [their plan] would have been weakened - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:39: Further, he should be careful of things of which it is said, "that which is crooked cannot be made straight" (Ecclesiastes 1:15) - explained in Midrash Rabbah (Parashat Naso 9:6), in these words: "if his wife go astray" - this is what is written, "he who commits adultery lacks understanding," and so on, "commits adultery" - this is what is written, "that which is crooked cannot be made straight," and so on. It is taught, "that which is crooked cannot be made straight" - this is one who has neglected the Shema of the morning or the Shema of the evening, or the morning prayer or the evening prayer; "and what is lacking cannot be counted" - this is one whose companions were counted in for a matter of a commandment, and he was not counted with them. And there they brought this mishnah taught in Chagigah (chapter 1, mishnah 7): Rabbi Shimon ben Menasya says, what is a "crooked thing that cannot be made straight"? This is one who has relations with a forbidden relative and begets a mamzer from her; if you say [it applies also] to a thief or a robber, he can still return it and rectify it. Further, there, in the mishnah: Rashbi says, one is called "crooked" only if he was once fit and then became crooked, and who is this? A Torah scholar who separates from the Torah.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:40: Also, he should be careful of what is explained in Midrash Rut, from the Zohar (page 78a), that "what is lacking cannot be counted" refers to the three words lacking in the Shema, to complete the 248 [words, corresponding to the 248 limbs], and the prayer leader repeats and says, "the LORD your God is true," to complete the 248 - and one who recites the Shema not with the community does not complete his 248 limbs, and of him it is said, "and what is lacking cannot be counted."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:41: And a penitent who fasts every day must be careful, on the days he eats, such as Shabbatot, festivals, and the New Moon, to eat only light things easy to digest - for a change in diet is the beginning of stomach illness - and even of good things he should not fill his belly, lest he fall ill and thereby neglect the Shema of morning or evening, which is a positive commandment of the Torah. And likewise public sanctification, which is a commandment, as it is written, "and I shall be sanctified among the children of Israel," as explained in the Zohar, Parashat Emor (page 93a). And likewise he stumbles when his companions are counted for a matter of a commandment, praying in the synagogue with ten, and he is not counted with them - and one accustomed to come to the synagogue, and one day he does not come, the Holy One, blessed be He, asks after him (cf. Berachot 6b). And also he does not complete the 248 words of the Shema, which is "a crooked thing that cannot be made straight." He also will neglect Torah study, which is a positive commandment of the Torah - and all this because of his foolishness, as he says (Proverbs 19:3), "the foolishness of man perverts his way," and so on.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:42: And the wise man's eyes are in his head, and he should be strong to conquer his inclination, and not be drawn after his desire - especially on the New Moon and Purim, when the feast is by the words of the Scribes, one must be careful not to fill his belly so much that he falls ill and comes to neglect Torah and prayer, which are positive commandments of the Torah - for a positive commandment of their words does not override a positive commandment of the Torah.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:43: The general rule is that the penitent must always be trembling and fearful of judgment, and not forget how much he has angered the Creator with his iniquities, and must fulfill, even on Shabbatot and festivals, "repent one day before your death" - for if he knew that on Shabbat or a festival he would die, how fearful and trembling he would be, and would rise early to read Torah, and would perform many good deeds, and would not be drawn after his pleasures. So he must do all his days, to repair what he has made crooked, on Shabbatot and festivals, and especially on days of joy, when a person is likely to be drawn after his pleasures and his inclination will seduce him - great care is needed, so that he not return to his old ways and be like a dog returning to its vomit, a fool repeating his folly - as has happened to many who returned to their old ways because of eating and drinking.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:44: Thus far is what our meager understanding has attained, in brief, of the words of our Rabbis and the Midrashim concerning repentance, and we did not wish to copy the words of the commentators so as not to lengthen it. The penitent needs all of them - especially the words of the Rokeach's repentances, which are words of tradition the penitent must perform, and likewise concerning the repentance for one who has relations with a married woman, spoken of in Sefer Chassidim (section 167), which the penitent must perform. And whoever wishes to perform complete repentance from heart and soul should not be negligent in seeking the books needed for the healing of his soul, just as a sick person is not negligent in seeking a doctor to heal him - and my words in this gate are only an awakening for the penitent; the things the earlier authors did not write, having left them as well known, are what I have written.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:45: And in any case, we saw fit to copy the repentances written in the book of Middot (cf. Orchot Tzaddikim, Gate 26) found among us, whose words appear to be words of tradition, in these words: and now the matters of affliction should be written according to each and every transgression. One who has relations with a gentile woman shall fast three days, night and day, three years, once a year - and if, Heaven forfend, after repentance he returns to his old ways, then it shall be made more and more severe upon him: in the summer days he shall go to a place with many ants and sit among them naked, and in the winter days he shall break the ice and sit in the water up to his nose - and if he returns to his old ways again, more shall be added upon him still further.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:46: One who emits seed in vain shall fast forty days, not consecutive, and sit in water in the winter days for as long as it takes to roast an egg, and during those forty days shall not eat meat, nor anything hot at night, nor drink wine, except on Shabbatot and festivals, and shall wash his head lightly with water two or three times during all those forty days.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:47: One who has relations with his menstruating wife shall fast forty consecutive days, and be lashed two or three times every day, and shall not eat meat, nor drink wine, nor eat anything hot, except on Shabbatot and festivals, and shall not bathe all those days, and shall confess every day. And if he embraced or kissed his menstruating wife, he shall fast forty days.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:48: One who kisses or embraces other women shall fast Monday, Thursday, and Monday, and shall distance himself from her doorway. And if he had relations with an animal, beast, or fowl, he shall fast forty days, and shall not bathe, and shall not look at an animal, beast, or fowl at the time they mate with one another.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:49: A murderer shall go into exile for three years, and shall be lashed in every single city, and say, "I am a murderer," and shall not eat meat nor drink wine, nor cut the hair of his head or beard, nor wash his garments, nor bathe his body - except that he shall wash his head once a month - and shall bind the hand with which he murdered, and his arm, in iron around his neck, and shall walk barefoot, and shall weep over his murder; and if a person reviles him, he shall be silent; and during those three years he shall not go on outings or engage in play, and in his exile he shall lay himself down before the entrance of the synagogue, and let all who pass by pass over him, but not tread upon him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:50: An apostate [who converted to another religion] shall remove his fine garments, and mourn, flee, and suffer all the days of his life, and humble his spirit and his pride, and confess three times every day, and shall not eat meat or drink wine except on Shabbatot and festivals, and shall not bathe, nor wash his head except once or twice a month, and shall not go to festivities or weddings except to hear the seven blessings alone, and shall not sit with idol-worshippers even in a place where words of Torah and commandments are spoken, and shall distance himself from their doorways, and shall not derive benefit from them - and as soon as he returns, he needs immersion, and shall endure suffering and affliction corresponding to his sins, for he denied the fundamental principle, and desecrated Shabbatot, and transgressed [sins punishable by] karet and death by the court - therefore he needs great suffering.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:51: One who has relations with a married woman or a betrothed young woman - he thereby forbids her to her husband, since she consented, and he is liable to death by the court for it - therefore he shall endure suffering as harsh as death, and sit in snow and ice one hour every day - so shall he do throughout the winter, every day, once or twice - and in the summer days he shall sit before flies or bees, or other suffering as harsh as death, and shall confess every day with weeping and sighing, and for a full year shall not eat meat nor drink wine except on Shabbat, festivals, and Purim, and shall not eat warm bread, and shall not bathe except lightly on the eves of festivals, and shall not watch any entertainment, though he may hear the blessings of bridegrooms, and shall not indulge himself in anything, and shall be lashed every day, and shall lie on the ground or on a bare board without a pillow or cushion - except that on Shabbat and festivals he may lie on straw and stubble with a pillow under his head - for he must remove his coarse spirit, from which desire came, and his life shall be a life of suffering, and he shall wear sackcloth on his flesh, and shall not speak of matters of desire for women, and shall not gaze at women or their ornaments even when not worn, and shall not listen to the sound of music, and shall not speak with women at all, neither by hint nor by gesture nor by anything - even with his own wife when she is menstruating, and shall not be secluded with her in any seclusion.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:52: One who swears falsely, or violates a ban, must be lashed several times all his days, and confess for many days, and afterward be careful not to swear even truthfully, neither by the Torah nor by the souls of his ancestors, but rather vow by the life of his own head - but he may swear to fulfill a commandment - and he should be careful not to utter the Name of Heaven in vain from his mouth, and his limbs should tremble when he mentions the Name, and he should be careful of a blessing in vain, and if he erred and recited a blessing in vain, he should say afterward, "blessed be the Name of His glorious kingdom forever and ever." And those who accustom themselves and their children to mention the Name of Heaven in the bathhouse and in a filthy place, mentioning the Name of Heaven in vain - woe to them, woe to their children, for thus have they taught their tongue! Therefore he should guard and fence himself, his children, and his companions who heed him, from mentioning the Name of Heaven in vain - and if this penitent needed to swear an oath to his creditor, even truthfully, he should fast that day every year.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:53: And if he was accustomed to speak of any matter in the synagogue, even not at the time of prayer, he should sit in great awe and pray with intention, and fast forty days, whether consecutive or spread out, and be lashed humbly every day.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:54: One who steals, or takes interest, should sit and ask forgiveness from him, and fast forty days or more, and confess every day, and be careful not to accept deposits, and not habitually go after his fellow's money, and perform acts of kindness with his body and his money, and give from his own to those who toil in Torah and fear Heaven. And this one who took interest, if he could have avoided taking interest even from gentiles, it would be good.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:55: One who informs against his fellow, making him hated in the eyes of the ruler, and slandering him, and taking his money, and killing his fellow and his wife and children who depend on him - he shall repay his fellow everything he lost, and ask his forgiveness, and be lashed and fast more than two years, and confess all the days of his life, for he is considered as though he killed his fellow's wife and children and his fellow, and committed many transgressions - therefore he shall break his spirit, and if he has nothing with which to pay, he shall increase [efforts to make] peace and ask his forgiveness, and economize, and repay him or his heirs.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:56: A talebearer and the like has no remedy until he asks his forgiveness, and is lashed, and fasts forty days or more and is lashed every day, and all his affairs should be occupied with commandments and the pursuit of peace between every person, and between every man and his wife.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:57: One who strikes his fellow, or causes him distress, whether through money or through wronging with words, has no atonement unless he appeases his fellow - for the Day of Atonement atones only for transgressions between him and the Omnipresent, but for those between him and his fellow, he must appease him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:58: One who raises his hand against his fellow is called wicked, and shall ask his forgiveness and be atoned for. One who shames his fellow's face shall fast forty days or more, and be lashed every day, and confess all the days of his life. One who gives his fellow a [derogatory] nickname shall ask his forgiveness publicly, and be lashed and fast forty days, and confess every day with humility.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:59: One who wrongs a convert shall ask his forgiveness, and be lashed and fast every day. One who provokes his fellow shall bring three rows of people and say, "I have sinned, I have straightened what I made crooked, though it did not benefit me," and ask his forgiveness three times, no more; and if he [the wronged party] has died, he shall bring ten people to his grave and say, "I have sinned against the LORD, God of Israel, and against so-and-so, whom I provoked" - and this is specifically where he did not disgrace him publicly, and mere appeasement was not sufficient from the start, and the one forgiving should not be cruel [in withholding forgiveness]. But if he provoked him and gave him a bad name, he has no eternal forgiveness unless he fasts and is lashed privately for forty days or more.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:60: One who profanes the Name - profanation of the Name is a great sin. And what is profanation of the Name? Rav said, such as I, who go to the butcher and take meat and do not pay immediately - meaning, he brings upon himself the disgrace of theft, and people learn from him and treat theft more lightly because of him. Rabbi Yochanan said, such as I, who walk four cubits without tefillin and without Torah, and people learn more from it. Rabbi Abahu said in the name of Rabbi Chanina ben Gamliel, it is better for a person to transgress in secret than to profane the Name of Heaven publicly - meaning, so that people not learn from his deeds.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:61: Rabbi Ila'i the Elder said, if a person sees that his inclination overpowers him, let him go to a place where he is not known, and dress in black, and do what his heart desires, and not profane the Name of Heaven publicly. And the Sages explained - Heaven forbid that they permitted him to transgress - rather, the Sages say that he should stand against his evil inclination since he desires nothing but to fulfill whatever is forbidden to him, and since he exiles himself far away and dresses in black, he shall then be broken and humbled and restrain his heart from sin - but to commit a forbidden act at all, not at all; rather, these deeds break the evil inclination and restrain it from transgressing, as Rabbi Ila'i said, for the toil of travel, the wearing of black, and being a stranger break the evil inclination and restrain it from transgression.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:62: And it says, whoever does not care for his Owner's honor, it would have been better for him not to have come into the world - and we say in the Gemara, Rav Yosef said, this is one who transgresses in secret, as Rabbi Yitzchak said - for Rabbi Yitzchak said, whoever transgresses in secret is as though he pushes against the feet of the Shechinah.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:63: Profanation of the Name is a transgression that bears fruit - when one does something bad, others learn from him. And of this transgression, every person should be very afraid, for profanation of the Name occurs in many ways and has no measure - for whoever belittles even one commandment and treats the honor of Heaven lightly is called a profaner of the Name, for others will learn from him and treat it more lightly and disdainfully.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:64: If a person transgressed [a sin warranting] karet or death by the court, repentance and the Day of Atonement atone half, and suffering atones half. But if the Name of Heaven was profaned through him, repentance has no power to suspend, nor the Day of Atonement to atone, nor suffering to cleanse - but all of these suspend, and death cleanses the iniquity. Therefore a person should be careful of profaning the Name and distance himself from what is unseemly and from what resembles it.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:65: And the essence of repentance for profanation of the Name is that he make his sins known before the many, and say to them, do not learn from me, for I have sinned, I have committed iniquity, I have transgressed, I have profaned the Name through my folly - and he fasts several fasts, and confesses every day until the day of his death.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:66: And for every single transgression a person commits, whether unwitting or intentional - such as touching a Shabbat candle, or lighting a candle on Shabbat and not remembering it is Shabbat, or doing it without his knowledge - he should confess and fast at least two days, Monday and Thursday. And so he should do for all the great transgressions a person commits - fast - and in this there are two benefits: the first, that the fast atones; and the second, that it restrains from transgressions, for he will think in his heart, if I do this I will need to fast, and thereby restrain himself from the transgression.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:67: And this is the great fence against all transgressions: that he fine himself, or give charity, or cause himself pain in his body when he has transgressed - and so he should do for all transgressions he is accustomed to, such as envy, hatred, joy [at another's misfortune], idle words, and slander, or not having intention in blessings and prayer, uttering blessings from his mouth without intention, and many similar things. And therefore he should examine himself every day concerning these matters - if he has encountered and transgressed one of them, he should hasten to suffer for them and confess whatever iniquity he has committed, seeking forgiveness from the Name with a broken heart.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:68: A great matter is confession, for our Rabbis taught: when one was about ten cubits from the place of stoning, they would say to him, "confess," for such is the way of those put to death, to confess - for whoever confesses has a share in the World to Come; and if he does not know how to confess, he should say, "may it be [Your] will that my death be an atonement for all my iniquities" - for so we find concerning Achan, to whom Joshua said (Joshua 7:19), "my son, give, I pray, glory to the LORD... and give Him thanks" - "and Achan answered and said, indeed I have sinned."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:69: All the commandments, whether positive or negative, if he transgressed one of them, whether willfully or unwittingly, when he repents of his sins he is obligated to confess before God, may He be exalted, as it is said (Numbers 5:7), "a man or woman who commit any of the sins of man," and so on, "then they shall confess their sin which they have done" - and this is the confession of words. And all those liable for sin-offerings and guilt-offerings, and all those liable for death by the court or lashes, are not atoned for through their death, their lashes, or their sacrifice, until they perform repentance and confess. And whoever injures or damages his fellow's money, even though he pays it, is not atoned for until he confesses and repents never to do such a thing again.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:70: And how shall he confess? He shall say: please, O Name, I have sinned, I have committed iniquity, I have transgressed before You, thus and thus I have done, and behold I regret and am ashamed of my deeds, and I shall never return to this thing again - and this is the essence of confession, that he not return to his old ways. And whoever increases in confessing and elaborates on this matter, this is praiseworthy. Also this is essential to confession, that he say, "but we have sinned." And it is very good to specify the sin within the confession - such as, if he ate carrion or torn animals or other forbidden things, he should specify it within his confession. How so? When he says "ashamti" [I have become guilty], he should say, I ate something impure. When he says "bagadti" [I have betrayed], if he had relations with a gentile woman or a married woman or a menstruant, he should say, I had relations. And if he stole or robbed, he should say, I have robbed. And if he gave his fellow a bad name, or spoke slander, or any excommunicable offense, he should say, I have spoken slander of him. And if he emitted seed in vain, he should say, I have committed iniquity. And if he committed adultery with forbidden relatives, he should say, I have acted presumptuously, I have committed harlotry. And if he desecrated Shabbatot or coveted, he should say, I have desecrated, I have coveted - and so for the whole alphabet, for each and every letter.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:71: And afterward he should specify, in his confession, the transgression he committed, and say, weeping, "let the wicked forsake his way, and the man of iniquity his thoughts" - and then it shall avail him. And the end of the confession: "I have turned away from Your good commandments and Your judgments, and it did not benefit me; and You are righteous concerning all that has come upon me, for You have acted truthfully, and I have done wickedly." And then he should say, thus I transgressed a positive commandment and negative commandments, and I transgressed [sins warranting] karet and death by the hand of Heaven, I transgressed [sins warranting] death by the court, and the Written Torah and the Oral Torah - I forgot Your great Name, I forgot the yoke of Your kingship and Your fear - and You are righteous concerning all, and so on.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:72: In the Yerushalmi (Yoma, chapter 8, halachah 9), it is explained how one should confess: he says, Master of the universe, I have done evil in Your eyes, and walked in the stubbornness of my heart, and did not heed Your reproof; may it be Your will, LORD my God and God of my fathers, that You atone for all my transgressions, and forgive me all my iniquities, and pardon me all my sins, and so on - to this point.
